title: Four missing western years have high local value for dating North Pacific oxygen loss in a ramp model
abstract: We test what records could improve the timing of North Pacific oxygen loss on sigma0 26.5. We use published annual within-type oxygen estimates in nine longitude bands for 1970-2025. A joint ramp fit adds only 0.414 percent to the residual-score reduction over a same-time decline; a conditional block test gives p=0.295. A fitted 0.14 year per degree signal is detected in 125 of 199 sampling-matched draws. A local nuisance-adjusted information calculation finds that four missing annual estimates at 160-170 E add 9.2 percent information at this delay, with separate regional ramp widths. Uniform annual sampling in all bands in 2026-2050 adds 53.8 percent, but needs 225 region-years. The western scenario gives 9.6 times more gain per added estimate; the ratio is 6.7 at the best-fit delay. This ranks hypothetical record recovery, not known samples. A stricter cruise filter retains only four bands and gives a positive gradient with p=0.025. Results depend on support, response shape and error assumptions. Code, licensed aggregate inputs, hashes, figures and reproduction checks are supplied.
